summary.headline: Digilogic FY26 revenue rose 8.4% to INR78.27 crore and PAT 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, but a ~INR22 crore spillover from delayed imported hardware missed the 20-25% growth guidance.
summary.overview: FY26 total income rose 8.4% YoY to INR78.27 crore, with EBITDA up 16.5% to INR15.18 crore and margin expanding 152 bps to 19.6%. PAT grew 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, and operating cash flow turned positive at INR12.63 crore. Management attributed the shortfall versus its January 2026 growth guidance to delayed imported OEM hardware, which pushed about INR22 crore of orders into FY27. Management guided to 20-25% growth for FY27, contingent on converting INR100-plus crore of orders by September 2026, and announced new subsidiary Abhedhya (RF systems), an SBC R&D effort, and Project UDAN manufacturing expansion.

segments.name: Measurement equipment
segments.commentary: About 49% of FY26 revenue; management said most of its value comes from software content with little material cost, supporting the margin gain.

segments.name: Checkout systems
segments.commentary: About 22% of FY26 revenue; ATEs about 17%. Management said ATE and checkout value was broadly flat YoY, and the share fell because measurement equipment grew.

segments.name: Prototyping vs production
segments.commentary: Management estimated roughly 30% of revenue from prototyping and 70% from production orders. This was not reconciled with a reported figure and was described as approximate.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25%, reiterated on the call; management said it is confident of meeting it.
Management targets INR100-plus crore of purchase orders by end-September 2026, with billing for FY27 expected to be supported by that order intake.
Order book was about INR30-plus crore as of 30 May 2026, with most expected to bill by August 2026.

Project UDAN (new manufacturing facility, about four times the current capacity) expected operational by mid-2028; indicative revenue INR11-13 crore in FY29, INR28-30 crore in FY30, INR57-61 crore in FY31.
Current setup capacity estimated at INR150-160 crore revenue potential.
Abhedhya (RF subsidiary) expected to demonstrate systems in 8-12 months; management indicated revenue in FY28, not FY27.
capex_capacity: Project UDAN: a manufacturing and environmental testing facility, about four times current size; mid-2028 target; can deliver 20-25 systems per six months versus about six currently.
Guest house under construction; capitalised finance cost on exposure of about INR2.1 crore (not fully drawn), borrowing at REPO plus 2.5%.
Abhedhya, a new RF subsidiary for radar, EW and communication subsystems, with a 1-year build-and-demonstrate timeline.
R&D: custom single board computer (SBC) built in-house by an eight-member team, about 1.5-2 years old; qualification range -20 to +85 degrees C; environmental testing not yet completed.
Management said two to three new R&D products are in development.
demand_pricing: FY26 execution was held back by imported hardware from US/European OEMs; lead time rose from about 2 months to about 4 months, leaving roughly INR22 crore spilled into April 2026. Management said about INR20 crore additional revenue would otherwise have closed in FY26.

Order book fell to about INR31 crore from INR46 crore; the tender pipeline fell to about INR110 crore from INR200 crore. Management attributed this to Government fund reallocation and said projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than lost.
Management said OEMs are rerouting shipments, adding a week or 10 days and roughly 1-2% cost.
Competitors named: Data Patterns and Zen Technologies, mainly in prototyping. Management said production work under DCPP is nomination-based with limited competition.
Customer base is 100% government in substance (DRDO, BDL, BEL, public sector defence production agencies), with some transactions billed through BDL.
Management said the export route is via DRDO and BDL systems, and MoUs with Sperry and Eirad are at the evaluation stage toward Tier-1 aerospace supply chains.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 guidance of 20-25% growth missed, and what supports FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported hardware arrived about 4 months after order rather than 2, leaving roughly INR22 crore of spillover. Management cited INR30-plus crore of orders in hand by 30 May and a target of INR100-plus crore of POs by September.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall from INR46 crore to INR31 crore and the pipeline from INR200 crore to INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said government fund reallocation changed priorities and projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than cancelled. The INR100-plus crore target covers only projects with budgets allocated or tenders out.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the revenue comes from production versus prototyping?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said roughly 30% prototyping and 70% production, and deferred exact figures to the CFO. No reported split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why set up Abhedhya as a separate company rather than a division?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RF work needs different people, salaries, infrastructure and design expertise than TMS, and separate accountability is needed. Tender qualification is to be built by demonstrating products first.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ATE and checkout share fall from about 44% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said measurement equipment, mostly software value add with low material cost, grew to a similar scale, and ATE and checkout value was broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the order book converting to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Current orders should bill by about August 2026. Pipeline orders are expected as POs by end-September, with 2-3 months of build and about one month of installation, and cash collection around Aug-Oct.

risks_watch: Import dependence: US and European OEM hardware lead times stretched to about 4 months, and a repeat would repeat the FY26 spillover.
Order book of INR31 crore against FY27 growth target; the INR100-plus crore PO target by September 2026 is the key checkpoint.
Tender pipeline down from INR200 crore to INR110 crore; delays of 6-8 months attributed to Government budget reallocation.
Revenue mix is a management estimate (30% prototyping, 70% production), not a reported figure.
Project UDAN and Abhedhya are not yet operational; Abhedhya revenue is expected only in FY28, and the SBC still needs environmental qualification.
Governance: management's FY26 growth guidance was missed, and the call shows the company's first results call as a newly listed SME.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 targets and on the causes of the FY26 miss, which management attributes to imported-hardware delays. Less specific on the revenue split, timelines for UDAN and Abhedhya, and the exact reasons for the pipeline fall. Several answers were deferred to the CFO or to a future call.
key_quotes: So, my target is by September, by September I should have purchase orders in hand close to INR100-plus crores, with which our billing will be comfortably meeting the targets which have been projected.

Imagine a scenario, everything would have gone in the right direction without this international disturbances had these items come on time, I would have comfortably closed additionally INR20 crores apart from INR76 crores what we have closed.
Only thing is that might get delayed by few months, maybe 6 to 8 months, which might spill over to subsequent financial year. But opportunities are not lost.
